questions.prompt: With 16×16 tiles, global loads per FMA drop from 2 to what?
questions.explanation: 2 / 16 = 0.125: each loaded element is used 16 times.

questions.prompt: Why are two __syncthreads() calls needed per k-step?
options: One after loading (so tiles are complete before use), one after computing (so nobody overwrites tiles still being read)
One for A and one for B
questions.explanation: A read-after-write barrier and a write-after-read barrier.

questions.prompt: In the shared-memory tiled kernel, about how many instructions are issued per FMA in the inner loop (two shared loads + the FMA)? What's the resulting ceiling as a % of peak?
Why does writing for (k = 0; k < 16; k++) rather than k < T matter in the simulator (and often on GPUs)?
options: With a literal trip count the loop is fully unrolled, so no branch is issued per iteration
questions.explanation: Compilers unroll loops whose trip count they can see.

questions.prompt: On a 128×128 GEMM with 16 SMs, why might 64×64 tiles be worse than 32×32?
options: Only 4 blocks for 16 SMs: most of the GPU idles
questions.explanation: Reuse is useless if the machine isn't full.
